title: PROP lifecycle close-on-verify is the same defect family as PROP-098 close_iss_batch. Tinker walks verification_pattern, acts on FAIL (logs STILL_BROKEN), never acts on PASS (close the PROP). Design auto-close mechanism.
context:
Operator-side observation 2026-06-14T16:20Z at the end of a 54-PROP-processed day. Across today's sweep, approximately two-thirds of the closures were 'already implemented — status was stale' (e.g., PROP-020 drift-audit ships in §7g + compute-drift-audit.js; PROP-037 'PROP-037 generalization (landed 2026-05-16)' explicitly written in decider-intake.md L66; PROP-088 audit-exp-tracker threshold change live in build-scripts/audit-exp-tracker-gaps.js L220-226; PROP-091/092 dome-mirror passes Phase 0 live in sync-workspace-step4c.js; etc.). The pattern is consistent: implementation work happens via decider patches / operator-cowork / amendment integrations, the PROP's verification_pattern starts returning FIXED — but the status field stays at 'proposed' or 'design-pending-operator-review' forever.

Key insight from the operator: this is the same one-sided-write defect family as PROP-098 close_iss_batch (closed today, commit 8fec33c). Tinker writes close_iss_batch HNOTEs; decider had no consumer; items sat 3+ runs. Same shape here: tinker authors PROPs and runs verification_pattern checks (per monitor/prompts/reference/tinker-proposals-and-fixes.md 'PROP Lifecycle Verification' section), but the closure side of the lifecycle has no writer. Tinker reports STILL_BROKEN when verification fails, but does NOTHING when verification passes.

Observed consequence: the unactioned-PROP pile became a structural demotivator for tinker authoring new proposals. Today's tinker reports explicitly noted 'standing candidates carried unactioned' for weeks — but many of those standing candidates HAD been implemented; tinker just had no auto-close mechanism to recognize the implementation and flip the status. The pile looks deep when it isn't.

Other-side check (operator already considered):
- Auto-close is a CHANGE TO PROP CANONICAL STATE. If verification_pattern is malformed or coincidentally passes for unrelated reasons, a real proposal could be incorrectly marked implemented. Conservative mitigation: only flip from a narrow set of statuses (e.g., 'proposed', 'design-pending-operator-review', 'pending-operator-review') and only when verification_pattern exits 0 cleanly with no ambiguity in output.
- Some PROPs have intentionally pending status because they require operator decision even if verification_pattern is satisfied (e.g., operator-approved-pending-rollout). Need an opt-out mechanism.
- Verification patterns vary in quality. Some are 'grep -q FOO file && echo FIXED || echo STILL_BROKEN' (good — pass/fail is unambiguous). Others are 'test -f X' alone (ambiguous — X might exist for unrelated reasons). Tinker needs a way to grade pattern quality before trusting it for auto-close.
- Operator-cowork-driven closures (like today's bulk sweep) write explicit obe_closure_note + obe_closure_evidence. Auto-closure should write equivalent metadata so the audit trail is uniform.
- Shadow-then-enforce rollout (the PROP-009 pattern) is the lowest-risk path. Phase 0: tinker logs what it WOULD close but doesn't write. Operator reviews logs for N days. Phase 1: enforce.
task: Design TWO mechanisms for PROP-lifecycle closure. Both address the close-bug operator surfaced 2026-06-14T16:30Z: 'these closures weren't superseded by luck — the work was deliberately done, just orphaned from the originating PROP.' Mechanism A — auto-close on verification_pattern pass — handles 'status stale despite original PROP's verification passing' (Case 1). Mechanism B — deliberate-supersedes annotation — handles 'underlying problem solved via a different path, original verification_pattern stays at STILL_BROKEN' (Case 2). Author both as PROP-NNN with phased rollout; if scope warrants, split into PROP-NNN and PROP-NNN+1 along the A/B boundary. Today's sweep showed both shapes: PROP-020/037/088/091/092 are Case 1 (verification passes against shipped code); PROP-008/012/063 are Case 2 (the structural problem was addressed via deliberate sibling work — PROP-019+020, lens system + PROP-038, PROP-087+089 — not coincidence). Both shapes need fixing for the operator-demotivator pattern to actually close.
investigation_questions: Q1 — Eligible status transitions. Which PROP statuses should be auto-flippable on verification pass? Conservative list (recommended): 'proposed', 'design-pending-operator-review', 'pending-operator-review', 'implementation-pending-operator-review'. Explicitly NOT auto-flippable: 'operator-approved' (operator gates rollout independent of verification), 'design-pending-operator-review' WITH 'requires_human_judgment: true' field set, anything with 'do_not_auto_close: true' opt-out flag set on the PROP itself. Map the inclusive list + the explicit denylist.

Q2 — Pattern quality grading. Verification patterns vary: 'grep -q PROP-NNN file && echo FIXED || echo STILL_BROKEN' (unambiguous), 'test -f X' (ambiguous — file may exist for unrelated reasons), 'curl ...' (network-dependent, never auto-close). Tinker should grade pattern quality and only trust grade-A patterns for auto-close. Grade-B (test-f only) emits a soft finding 'PROP-NNN verification passed but pattern is ambiguous; manual review recommended'. Define the grading rubric.

Q3 — Closure metadata. When tinker auto-closes, what does it write? Recommended (mirrors today's bulk-close pattern): obe_closed_at (ISO), obe_closed_by ('tinker-auto-close-2026-06-14T...'), obe_prior_status (the previous status), obe_closure_note ('Auto-closed via verification_pattern at tinker-RUN_ID; pattern exited 0 with FIXED in output'), obe_closure_evidence (the literal verification_pattern command + its output). This makes operator-cowork bulk closures and tinker auto-closures use the same schema.

Q4 — Audit log. Mirror PROP-026's closure-ledger.jsonl pattern. Tinker writes one JSON line per auto-close (or candidate-close in shadow mode) to monitor/tinker/prop-auto-close-ledger.jsonl. Schema: {ts, run_id, prop_id, prior_status, new_status, verification_pattern, verification_output, pattern_grade, dryrun: bool}. Classified git-append-only per PROP-065. Tinker reads this on subsequent runs to detect any over-eager close (cross-check operator complaints).

Q5 — Opt-out mechanism. Some PROPs may pass verification mechanically but have substantive operator-decision content (e.g., a PROP that proposes both an implementation AND an operator policy change — the implementation can ship without the policy decision being made). Add 'do_not_auto_close: true' as an opt-out flag PROPs can set. Tinker honors it. Document in CLAUDE.md (or wherever PROP schema is canonicalized) so PROP authors know about the flag.

Q6 — Shadow-then-enforce rollout. PROP-009r2 used this pattern (shadow mode writes prop-009-shadow.jsonl for N days, operator audits, then enforce mode flips a flag). Mirror it here: Phase 0 (shadow) — tinker walks PROPs, runs verifications, logs what it WOULD close, writes 0 changes to PROP files. Phase 1 (enforce after operator audit) — tinker auto-closes from a flag like monitor/tinker/prop-auto-close-enforce.flag (presence = enforce, absence = shadow). Same pattern as monitor/decisions/prop-009-enforce.flag.

Q7 — Frequency. Tinker runs once daily. Should auto-close run every run, every Mode 3, or on a separate cadence? Recommended: every run as part of the pre-flight (cheap — one grep per PROP × ~80 PROPs is sub-second). Surfacing N auto-closes per run in latest-tinker-summary.txt gives operator visibility without adding cost.

Q8 — Out of scope. Tinker should NOT auto-close PROPs that require an operator decision beyond verification (e.g., choosing between two options, approving a policy). Those PROPs typically have requires_human_judgment: true OR have multiple recommendation branches the operator must pick between. Auto-close is for the simple 'work shipped, status was stale' case — exactly the 27/54 pattern today's sweep surfaced.

Q9 — Mechanism B (deliberate-supersedes annotations). PROP-008 was closed today as 'superseded by PROP-019 + PROP-020' — its structural intent (curmudgeon Priority 3 cooldown) was deliberately addressed by the PROP-019 reduced-set fingerprint + PROP-020 precompute pattern. Verification_pattern on PROP-008's original cooldown-gate proposal still returns STILL_BROKEN because the gate spec never landed verbatim. Mechanism A misses this entirely. Mechanism B: add a `supersedes_props: ['PROP-008']` field convention to NEW PROPs at authorship time (so when PROP-019 is authored, the author declares 'this supersedes PROP-008'). Tinker's auto-close walks this graph: if PROP-019 is implemented AND PROP-019.supersedes_props includes PROP-008, auto-close PROP-008 as 'superseded-by-PROP-019' with verification metadata pointing at PROP-019. Could also support reverse: 'superseded_by_props: ['PROP-019']' on PROP-008 written retroactively. Discipline question: this requires PROP authors to be diligent about declaring supersedes_props at authorship. Worth it because it makes the graph machine-readable and auto-closable.

Q10 — Manual sibling-supersedes flag for retroactive coverage. Even with Q9 discipline on new PROPs, the existing backlog has PROPs whose supersession was operator-detected today via manual review (PROP-008/012/063). Add a manual operator-side annotation tool — `monitor/scripts/mark-prop-superseded.js PROP-008 by PROP-019 PROP-020` — that writes the supersedes_by_props field plus the standard obe_* closure metadata. Lower-friction than editing the JSON by hand. Optional but reduces the cost of the next manual sweep.
deliverable: A PROP-NNN proposal in monitor/tinker/proposals/ with: (1) Q1 eligible-status whitelist + denylist; (2) Q2 pattern-grading rubric (grade A/B/C with explicit criteria); (3) Q3 closure-metadata schema (mirrors today's bulk-close pattern for uniformity); (4) Q4 audit-log JSONL schema + classification; (5) Q5 opt-out flag mechanism; (6) Q6 shadow-then-enforce rollout plan; (7) Q7 frequency decision with cost estimate; (8) Q8 out-of-scope boundary; (9) bonus — Phase 0 shadow-mode dry-run output: walk every PROP currently in monitor/tinker/proposals/, log what auto-close WOULD do, surface the count of would-be-closures so operator can sanity-check the design against today's just-closed corpus. Propose-only; operator integrates after review.
constraints: Do NOT design a mechanism that auto-closes from 'operator-approved' or 'integrated' statuses. Those are terminal operator decisions; verification passing does not override them.

Do NOT skip the shadow phase. Today's 54-PROP-processed-day showed how easy it is to get closure decisions wrong (e.g., PROP-005 partially-addressed-by-cadence-shift vs implemented vs deferred — same evidence supports any of three dispositions depending on framing). Shadow mode gives operator a chance to catch this before enforcement.

Honor the other-side: the diagnosis 'tinker is demotivated by the unactioned pile' is operator inference. The actual cause may also be that some PROPs genuinely sit unactioned (PROP-021 from a year ago is real). Don't over-attribute today's pattern to the close-bug alone; the demotivation is multi-factor. Auto-close addresses the close-bug factor specifically.

Mirror PROP-098's idempotency discipline. Auto-close must be safe to run twice in a row — second run sees status already flipped, no-ops cleanly. Pattern: check current status before flipping, only flip if currently in the auto-flippable whitelist.
Audit-log writes go to monitor/tinker/prop-auto-close-ledger.jsonl via clone-and-push (PROP-065 git-append-only). Register in build.js OWNERSHIP + workspace-sync.md GIT_APPEND_ONLY + CLAUDE.md.

not_in_scope: Retroactively closing today's 27 stale-status PROPs — that was operator-cowork-driven today.
Generalizing auto-close to other artifact classes (ISS, EXP, ATT items). Those have different lifecycle mechanisms and different writers.
Verification pattern QUALITY improvements — many existing patterns are 'echo FIXED' shape, some are weaker. Q2 grades them but does NOT rewrite them. Pattern improvements are separate PROPs.
Mode 3 vs Mode 4 placement decision — let tinker design where this lives. Recommended Mode 4 because that's the proposals-and-fixes module, but the pre-flight is also defensible.
